newsitem.title: CROATIA: U.S. arms for Bosnia arrive in Balkans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. arms for Bosnia arrive in Balkans.

text.p: A chartered ship carrying the bulk of a $100 million arms shipment for the Moslem-Croat federation in Bosnia arrived in the port of Ploce in neighbouring Croatia on Thursday, U.S. officials said.
The unloading of weaponry including tanks and helicopters was to begin on Friday and last two to three days, a U.S. official with the American "Train and Equip" programme said.
Officials said the arms will then be transported overland to storage sites in neighbouring Bosnia.

The programme, combining military hardware and instruction for federation army troops, was devised to ensure a parity of forces in the region and help the federation army counter any future threat from its Serb foes.
European powers have criticised Washington's patronage of Moslem-Croat forces, saying it undermined diplomatic goals to promote reconciliation and arms control in Bosnia.

The Moslem-led Bosnian army was outgunned by Serb forces during the 43-month war and had to rely on Islamic countries such as Iran for arms shipments, which violated an international arms embargo on former Yugoslavia.

A special "roll on-roll off" freighter chartered by the U.S. Military Sealift Command, a wing of the Defence Department, arrived in Ploce harbour on Friday morning with the main package of the Train and Equip scheme.

On board were 45 M60A3 main battle tanks, 15 UH-1H helicopters, 840 AT-4 light anti-tank weapons, 800 M60 machine guns, 80 armoured personnel carriers and 45,100 M-16 rifles. All weapons had ammunition with them.
There was also communications, power and training equipment, U.S. officials said.
In August, the United States sent a symbolic advance shipment of 1,000 M-16 rifles, 200 M60 machine guns, associated ammunition and 200 tactical radios.
Instruction of Bosnian soldiers began in October when a team of 170 retired U.S. officers, hired by the federation authorities, launched a training programme near Sarajevo.
The retired officers, from the private firm MPRI based in Alexandria, Virginia, also started field training of two Bosnian army brigades.
